content.text: What is the difference between the personal CI and the workstation CI?
I’ll check the repository’s CI workflows and documentation to compare them. I’m using the directory-structure skill to locate those files.

The main difference is **manual testing on your computer versus automatic testing on a shared team workstation**. They use the same underlying test pipeline.

| | Personal CI | Team workstation CI |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | You explicitly select a PR or candidate/baseline pair | Automatically discovers `main` and PRs targeting `main`; also supports manual runs |
| Jenkins structure | One parameterized job | A multibranch job with separate PR jobs |
| Workflow source | Trusted pipeline from `main` | Controller-owned bootstrap loads trusted workflow from `main` |
| GitHub status | Separate status per personal machine | Shared `team-workstation` status |
| Access | Local Jenkins, normally port 8080 | Workstation Jenkins on loopback port 8082, accessed remotely through SSH |
| Intended use | Checks you choose to run | Ongoing team CI and potentially a merge gate |

**Test coverage is shared:** the workstation workflow actually loads `jenkinsfile.personal`, forwarding its workstation configuration. Both build candidate and baseline dependencies, run unit tests, compare serial and parallel C regressions, and publish reports. Hardware and selected machine configuration can differ.

See the [personal setup](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/README.personal.md) and [workstation setup](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/README.team_workstation.md).
